The surah begins by addressing the source of prophethood and of this belief and creed.

﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people﴾ (17:1). That is, the source of guidance and prophethood is the Divine Being. All the prophets take their beliefs and instructions from Allah. Allah is the Creator of human beings and of this universe, and it is Allah who placed within the nature of humankind the capacity to recognize the Lord. Whenever people turned away from the path of their natural disposition (fitrah) and from Allah's guidance, Allah sent some messenger. All the messengers always turned the humanity that had lost its way back onto the straight path.

Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) was the first link in the chain of messengers, that is, after Prophet Adam (peace be upon him). The Qur'an does not mention Prophet Adam's prophethood in terms of what he did to guide people, because Prophet Adam was charged only with guiding his sons and grandsons. After the death of Prophet Adam, his grandsons and descendants went astray after a period of time and fashioned idols for themselves and began to worship them. At first they used these as a means of attention to sacred powers, but later they adopted the worship of the idols themselves. Among these idols, the most famous were the five idols mentioned in this surah. When these people went astray, Allah first sent Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) to guide them. Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) made a long effort to bring them back to the creed of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and worked to correct their beliefs.

In earlier scriptures, Prophet Idris (peace be upon him) is mentioned as the first prophet, that is, even before Prophet Noah (peace be upon him). However, the contents of earlier scriptures are not authoritative for us, because they have been repeatedly distorted, and material has repeatedly been deleted and added to them.

The study of the stories in the Qur'an gives the same impression: that Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) was the first prophet, and that he was sent at the very beginning of humanity. Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) preached for nine hundred and fifty years. The long lifespan of the people of that age also indicates that they belonged to a very early period, and at that time the number of human beings was also very small, and the human race had not yet spread as it did in later times. The study of biology shows that when the number of individuals is small, lifespan is longer. Allah alone knows the reality. This is our inference based on the study of the divine laws (sunan Ilahi).

After this, there is a brief indication of the mission and objective of Prophet Noah's (peace be upon him) prophethood, namely that O Noah (peace be upon him), you should warn your people:

﴿That you warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment﴾ (17:1). Given the state to which the people of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) had reached, and the way in which they were turning away from his instructions and preaching, growing arrogant and afflicted with extreme obstinacy and hostility, it is appropriate here to say simply that you should warn them of an evil end. Accordingly, he began his address by saying: O people, fear the punishment of this world and the Hereafter; you are making yourselves deserving of this punishment.

Immediately after the determination of the duty of prophethood, it is told that Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) had already begun preaching. His address was that, O people, although you have committed most heinous crimes, still turn back, repent, and your sins will be forgiven and your reckoning will be postponed until the Day of Resurrection. Otherwise, you deserve immediate destruction and seizure. Along with this, the principle of the call was also mentioned: worship Allah alone, and follow my way in all matters.

Allah says: ﴿He said: "O my people! Indeed I am to you a plain warner, that you worship Allah, fear Him and obey me. He will forgive you your sins and defer you to an appointed term. Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not postponed, if only you knew."﴾ (71:2-4)

﴿He said: "O my people! Indeed I am to you a plain warner."﴾ (71:2) In his call, what Nuh clarifies is the warning, and he explains this warning with great clarity. He does not speak in vague terms, nor does he speak through complicated, roundabout hints and allusions, nor does he hedge about his call. He also made plain the fate that the people of Nuh were about to face: that if they turned back, the punishment of this world could be deferred.

Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) presented a call that was also simple and straightforward.

﴿That you worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me﴾ (71:3). That is: worship Allah alone and do not associate anything with Him, do not fear anyone other than Allah, let this be what dominates your consciousness and conduct, and obedience to the Messenger of Allah is that from which a system of life springs forth and the detailed principles of life are formulated, which is expressed through the Sunnah of the Messenger.

Thus these are the outlines of all the heavenly religions: the command of Allah and obedience to the Messenger of Allah. Religion is established on these very lines. The details vary according to the circumstances of each age. Differences arise in the details and branches of religions as a result of the answers to humanity's detailed questions, its conception of existence, and the various questions that arise in different eras about this universe.

Wholeheartedly worshipping Allah is in fact itself a complete system. In the worship of Allah are included the concept of divinity, the details of obedience to Him, the nature of the relationship between Creator and creation, the principles of good and evil in this universe, and the principles of good and evil in people's lives. In this way, a complete system of life is established from the principle of worshipping Allah. A method of living life comes to the fore. This is a divinely ordained way of life, and from it one learns what the relationship between servitude and divinity is, and what the values are that Allah has prescribed concerning living and non-living things. And "the fear of Allah" is the guarantor that sustains this system of life and way of life. A people in whose hearts is the fear of Allah does not deviate from this way, nor does it seek excuses and pretexts. Moreover, through taqwa (God-consciousness), noble morals also arise within a person. A person's conduct becomes genuine, without any show or display.

Obedience to the Messenger in fact determines the boundaries of the path, and a person derives detailed guidance for walking this straight path and remains directly connected to the Lord, the Exalted, and the higher realm.

These were the outlines upon which Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) established the path of guidance and the way of life for people from the beginning of humanity. And all the calls of the subsequent eras continued to be founded upon these same lines, and Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) promised his people that if they repented and returned, Allah would forgive them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verse 4:

﴿...and He will forgive you your sins and defer you until an appointed term.﴾ (17:4 in the source numbering) And this respite will be in exchange for your worshipping Allah, fearing Allah, and obeying the Messenger of Allah. In return, Allah will further forgive your past sins, and your reckoning will be deferred until the time Allah has appointed, namely the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Akhirah). In this way, the destructive punishment that was coming upon you in this world will also be deferred. (Soon Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) will present that Allah had made other promises to these people as well.)

After this it is said that the establishment of the Hour is certain, and it will surely come at its appointed time. It cannot be delayed, unlike the punishment of this world, which can be delayed. Thus, the belief about the Hereafter is corrected in this way.

﴿Indeed, when the term appointed by Allah comes, it is not deferred; if only you knew.﴾ (17:4 in the source numbering) By this may be meant the Hour, and it may also mean any other time that Allah appoints for the occurrence of an event. In any case, the aim here is to instill the general belief that the term appointed by Allah cannot be averted. Yes, if these people obey and repent, Allah will defer their punishment until the Establishment of the Hour instead of destroying them in this world.

Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) continues his efforts and strives to guide his people. He does not care for any expediency and does not consider any personal gain. He endures everything for this great purpose. People object, turn away and mock him, but he keeps his work going. Nine hundred and fifty years pass in this struggle. Only a few people accept the call, while the people's turning away, their insistence on misguidance, and their mockery only increase. Exactly after nine hundred and fifty years, Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) presents his report of performance in the court of Allah the Exalted. He tells of whatever happened during this long period, although the Lord already knows it. Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) also knows that the Lord knows, yet the complaint is repeated in this way, and the complaint of the prophets can only be directed to Allah. They can present their plea only before Allah. And those believers who attain the reality of faith also complain only to Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 5–6:

قال رب انی ............................ سبلا فجاجا

This was the performance of Prophet Nuh (عليه السلام), and this is his report. In this long period of performance, he presents his account before his Lord. What stands out in his report is his continuous struggle.

إني دعوت ... وَنَهَارًا (71:5) "O my Lord! I have called my people night and day."

They did not lose heart, did not pause, and despite their constant turning away and obstinacy, they did not despair of the people. But

فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَائِي إِلَّا فِرَارًا (71:6) "But my call only increased them in flight."

That is, they kept fleeing from the one calling to Allah, and clung to Satan. Yet Allah was their Creator, and the blessings in which they were living comfortably were created by Allah. This guidance too was coming from Allah, and the caller sought neither reward nor charged any fee. And the One from whom they were fleeing was calling them so that they might be forgiven, so that they might be saved from the consequences of their sins, and saved from disobedience and misguidance.

They kept running away, but the callers to truth kept surrounding them and conveyed the word of truth to their ears in every way. Yet they neither tolerated the word of truth entering their ears, nor liked that their eyes should fall upon the Prophet. Therefore they persisted in misguidance with great stubbornness and showed great arrogance in refusing to accept the word of truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 7–8:

"And every time I called them, that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted in their refusal, and grew arrogant with great arrogance." (71:7)

This is the manner of the caller to truth: he insists upon his call, and whenever and as often as he gets the opportunity, he speaks the word of truth. At the same time, this is also an example of the persistence of the disbelievers: when they adopt obstinacy, they even cover their faces. From this call and this refusal it becomes clear that in the early days, when humanity was in its childhood, what were the days and nights of the call, that people would put their fingers in their ears and hide their heads under their sheets. The manner of expression makes the disbelieving conduct of the people apparent. Noah (peace be upon him) says that they put their fingers into their ears. Whole fingers are not actually pushed into the ears, but this was said for emphasis, that they were closing their ears in such a way that no sound could reach their ears in any way. It is as if they were trying to push their whole fingers into their ears. This is a form of severe insistence and obstinacy, and in the early periods this was the state of affairs.

Along with continuous preaching, taking advantage of every opportunity, and tireless effort, Prophet Nuh (عليه السلام) also adopted every method of calling to Islam (da'wah, the invitation to Islam). At times he called people openly and publicly. At other times he carried on a secret campaign.

﴿Then indeed I called them openly. Then I announced to them, and I spoke to them in private, in secret.﴾ (17:9)

During this call, Prophet Nuh (عليه السلام) also told them that if they accepted his message, they would attain success in both worlds, this world and the Hereafter. He also told them that if they sought forgiveness for their sins, Allah would forgive them, for He is indeed very forgiving.

"So I said: 'Ask your Lord for forgiveness; indeed He is Ever-Forgiving.' ﴿Verily He is ever Forgiving﴾ (71:10). ... [rest of passage follows]" — no, let me translate the given text only.

Surah Nuh (71), verse 10:

"I said: 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord, for indeed He is ever Oft-Forgiving,' ﴿He will send down on you abundant rain from the sky, and provide you with wealth and children, and make for you gardens and make for you rivers﴾ (71:10–12). And he held out to them the enticement that Allah would give them abundant provision, would send rivers flowing through the rains, would give them children and wealth, which are very dear to them."

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 11–12:**

﴿He will send down abundant rain upon you from the sky, will provide you with wealth and children, will make gardens for you, and will make rivers flow for you.﴾ (17:11) ... (17:21)

Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) combined seeking forgiveness (istighfar) with the granting of provision. The Qur'an, in numerous places, joins faith, guidance, righteousness, piety, prosperity and abundant provision with one another. Elsewhere it says:

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heavens and the earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they had earned.﴾ (7:69)

And elsewhere:

﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have removed their misdeeds from them and admitted them to gardens of bliss. And if they had established the Torah, the Gospel, and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾ (5:56–66)

And elsewhere:

﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed I am to you a warner and a bringer of good news from Him, and that you seek forgiveness from your Lord and turn to Him in repentance, and He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term, and will give every person of merit his merit.﴾ (11:2–3)

This principle, which the Qur'an mentions at various places, is a sound principle. It rests on Allah's promise and on the laws of life that Allah has established in this universe, and the practical history of humankind bears witness to it as a just witness. This rule applies to nations, not to individuals. In this world, whenever a nation has built its system upon the Shariah, adopted righteous deeds, adopted an attitude of fear of God, and sought forgiveness from Allah for its shortcomings, Allah has also granted it material progress. In short, whenever a nation has adopted piety, served Allah, implemented the Shariah, and established a system of justice among people, the natural forces of this universe have cooperated with it, Allah has granted it authority (tamkin) on earth, and it has reached the heights of worldly progress.

Sometimes we see on this earth nations that do not fear Allah and do not act in accordance with the Shariah of Allah, yet they are granted abundant provision. And they are also given supreme authority over the earth. But this too is a trial from Allah.

﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial.﴾ Then this prosperity is a rotten prosperity, and it is afflicted with flaws such as collective diseases, moral corruption, oppression and transgression, and the lack of human nobility, and its taste is bitter. Today before us are two great powers to whom Allah has given such expansion in provision. Authority over a large part of the earth has been given to them. One is capitalist and one is communist. (Sayyid Qutb, Allah may have informed you that this has already perished.) As for the first, its moral condition is lower than that of animals. The overall state of its life is that it stands only on the dollar, and apart from the dollar there is no moral value there. And in the second government, the human being is lower than a slave, and its system of espionage is so terrifying that every person lives in constant fear. No one sleeps at night without fear that he will be arrested in the morning. Both these countries are fallen by human standards. (Only Stalin put 30 million people to the sword. Translator.)

Now consider how Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) persisted in his long struggle. We see that he invites his people to the proofs of faith found within themselves and in the horizons. He is astonished at how the people respond by rejecting him, adopting a most insolent attitude. He rebukes them for this attitude.

﴿What is the matter with you, that you do not expect dignity from Allah?﴾ (71:13) ﴿And He has created you in stages.﴾ (71:14) "What is the matter with you that you do not hope for reverence from Allah, while He has created you in various stages?" What were these stages? Did the people of Nuh (peace be upon him) understand them well, or did they have a meaning which they understood well at that time, and this variation and distinction had a very good effect on their minds? Reflecting upon it, they could have come onto the right path. The opinion of most exegetes (tafsir, explanation of the Qur'an) is that the intended meaning is the various stages of the embryo: nutfah (drop), 'alaqah (clinging clot), mudghah (lump of flesh), and the present form of the human body. These people also understood this reality, and so do we, because those whose embryos would fall before they were complete would have observed these human stages through their observation. Nevertheless, this is one of the possible meanings of this verse. It is also possible that the intended meaning is the stages of the embryo, that at the beginning it becomes a single-celled creature, then a creature of many cells, then like aquatic creatures, then like mammals, and finally in the present shape of the human being. But these stages were not easily comprehensible to the people of Nuh (peace be upon him), because these stages have only recently been observed. And its meaning may also be that of other verses.

﴿Then We developed it into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾ (23:14) It is also possible that these two verses have some other meaning besides this, which we have not yet been able to understand and may understand at some later time.

In any case, Nuh (peace be upon him) directed them to the study of their own selves and sharply challenged them: look and see how Allah has created you, and yet people do not recognize the Creator, although they see that among all creatures the human being is a marvelous creation. After this, Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) directs them to the universe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 15–16:

Alam tarau ... siraja (71:15–16): "Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens, one above another, and made the moon a light in them and the sun a lamp?"

We cannot determine the meaning of the seven heavens according to the scientific theories that scientists keep constructing about this universe, because scientific theories are hypotheses.

Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) drew the people's attention to the seven heavens, and Allah informed him that they are seven. In these heavens, the sun and the moon are such that one is a light and the other is a lamp. People were looking at the heavens, and they were also looking at the sun and the moon. The heaven is described as the atmosphere, which is bluish. What is it? Neither could they know its reality, nor was it required of them, and to this day its reality has not become known. This degree of explanation is sufficient for a person to reflect upon this awe-inspiring universe and see how wondrously the power of Allah has created it, and this was the very purpose of Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him).

After this, Nuh (peace be upon him) draws their attention to how Allah created you from the earth, how He returns you to the earth, and then how He will bring you out from it again.

After this, Nuh (peace be upon him) draws their attention to how Allah created you from the earth, how He returns you to the earth, and then how He will bring you out from it again.

Allah has caused you to grow from the earth in a wondrous manner (17). Then He will return you into it, and will bring you forth again, (bringing you out) with a sudden emergence (18).

The process of human creation is expressed here as "growing," and this is a remarkable manner of expression. The Qur'an adopts this mode of expression in a number of places. For example:

﴿And the good land brings forth its vegetation by the permission of its Lord, while that which is inferior comes forth only sparsely﴾. This verse alludes to the creation of human beings. The mention of the creation of plants alongside the creation of humans occurs in many places. In Surah al-Hajj, while presenting an argument for resurrection after death, it is said:

﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [We develop you] that you may reach your maturity. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every beautiful kind﴾. And in Surah al-Mu'minun, while describing the various stages of creation, it is also mentioned:

﴿Then We caused it to grow into gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, and similarly in other places.

This is a feature worthy of attention. It shows that Allah has established nearly the same principles for life and vegetation upon the surface of the earth. The creation of man is similar to the creation of plants. The elements from which man is created are the same from which animals and plants are also created. Both draw their nourishment from these same elements. Man and animals are themselves among the vegetation of the earth. Just as Allah has given plants variety and diversity, so too has He given variety and diversity to animals and humans. Both are from the earth, both take sustenance from the earth, and both return to dust in the earth.

Thus, through faith, a believer's consciousness develops a correct conception of the living beings that grow upon this earth. This is a living and vivid consciousness, because its foundation is conscious faith, and this is the distinctive feature of Qur'anic knowledge.

Those who have been created from the earth return into its womb. Just as Allah brought them forth from the earth, He will return them to the earth again. Accordingly, He will bring out their bones and decayed remains, the particles of the earth, from the earth. And this will happen in the same way as it happened the first time. This is an extremely easy task for Allah. He will accomplish it in a moment, in a twinkling of an eye. This matter is easily understood, provided people reflect on this reality from the Qur'anic perspective.

Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) drew his people's attention to this reality, so that they would know that Allah is the Possessor of power, that He caused you to grow from this earth and will again bring you forth in the same way. When this awareness settles within a person, he begins to fear the Hereafter and prepares for it, for this Resurrection will be established as easily as plants grow upon this earth, with perfect ease and facility, leaving no room for any reasonable person to argue or dispute.

Allah has caused you to grow from the earth in a wondrous manner (17). Then He will return you into it, and will bring you forth again, (bringing you out) with a sudden emergence (18).

The process of human creation is expressed here as "growing," and this is a remarkable manner of expression. The Qur'an adopts this mode of expression in a number of places. For example:

﴿And the good land brings forth its vegetation by the permission of its Lord, while that which is inferior comes forth only sparsely﴾. This verse alludes to the creation of human beings. The mention of the creation of plants alongside the creation of humans occurs in many places. In Surah al-Hajj, while presenting an argument for resurrection after death, it is said:

﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [We develop you] that you may reach your maturity. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every beautiful kind﴾. And in Surah al-Mu'minun, while describing the various stages of creation, it is also mentioned:

﴿Then We caused it to grow into gardens of palm trees and grapevines﴾, and similarly in other places.

This is a feature worthy of attention. It shows that Allah has established nearly the same principles for life and vegetation upon the surface of the earth. The creation of man is similar to the creation of plants. The elements from which man is created are the same from which animals and plants are also created. Both draw their nourishment from these same elements. Man and animals are themselves among the vegetation of the earth. Just as Allah has given plants variety and diversity, so too has He given variety and diversity to animals and humans. Both are from the earth, both take sustenance from the earth, and both return to dust in the earth.

Accordingly, He will bring out their bones and decayed remains, the particles of the earth, from the earth. And this will happen in the same way as it happened the first time. This is an extremely easy task for Allah. He will accomplish it in a moment, in a twinkling of an eye. This matter is easily understood, provided people reflect on this reality from the Qur'anic perspective.

When this awareness settles within a person, he begins to fear the Hereafter and prepares for it, for this Resurrection will be established as easily as plants grow upon this earth, with perfect ease and facility, leaving no room for any reasonable person to argue or dispute.

Finally, Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) draws the people's attention to the facilities that Allah has created for them within the earth. He made the earth subservient and tractable for them, and placed within it all the means for their survival.

﴿And Allah has made the earth a spread-out carpet for you, that you may traverse within it broad roads.﴾ (71:19–20)

This truth, which Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) presented before the people and which was right in front of them, was something they could flee from in his words, but the realities contained within it were difficult for them to escape. This earth lay spread out before them. These mountains existed, these valleys existed, and it was along the paths of these valleys that they walked. They walked on foot, they travelled riding, and they travelled swimming. And the bounties and favours of Allah scattered within it, they benefited from, and they benefited from them with great ease.

These realities they were seeing with their own eyes; no deep scholarly research was needed in this regard. These were principles of nature, within their observation and experience, and they were living within these realities. Yes, as humanity advanced in knowledge, it discovered further aspects of these realities, concerning which the guidance of the Qur'an also says: travel through the earth and take admonition.

﴿He it is who has made the earth tractable for you, so walk in its broad paths and eat of His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 67:15)

Thus Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) strove to place the word of wisdom into the ears of his people somehow or other, through various methods and various styles; he adopted different approaches for this and devoted a long period to this work, with patient perseverance and tireless effort, for nine hundred and fifty years, continuously! After this, Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) returns to his Lord, the Lord who had given him this mission, and presents his report. This report is extremely detailed. It is in an extremely painful tone and in extremely effective words. From this account it becomes clear how much effort he exerted. He did everything he could to bring humanity, which had lost its way, back onto the path of guidance. But this is only one link in the chain of prophethood.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 20–21:

Qal Nuh... [the passage begins with the Qur'anic quotation "قال نوح" and continues to "الا ضلاً"]

The summary of Prophet Nuh's (peace be upon him) lament is that his people rejected him completely despite his long struggle and continuous effort. Despite presenting the truth well and shedding clear light on the realities, the people turned away. They were warned, and they were also promised wealth, property, power, and children. They were enticed with the prospect of progress and prosperity. Since these people followed misguided leaderships, and misguided leaderships always deceive their people, because misguided leaderships hold financial resources and status and power, people follow exactly those leaders.

Wa-ittaba'u... [the Qur'anic quotation "واتبعوا" continues to "خسارا" (17:12)] "and they followed those (chiefs) who, having been given wealth and children, have only increased in ruin." This wealth and these children deceived them and led them further astray. Consequently, through wealth and children, they received only misfortune and loss.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verses 20–21:

Qal Nuh... [the passage begins with the Qur'anic quotation "قال نوح" and continues to "الا ضلاً"]

The summary of Prophet Nuh's (peace be upon him) lament is that his people rejected him completely despite his long struggle and continuous effort. Despite presenting the truth well and shedding clear light on the realities, the people turned away. They were warned, and they were also promised wealth, property, power, and children. They were enticed with the prospect of progress and prosperity. Since these people followed misguided leaderships, and misguided leaderships always deceive their people, because misguided leaderships hold financial resources and status and power, people follow exactly those leaders.

Wa-ittaba'u... [the Qur'anic quotation "واتبعوا" continues to "خسارا" (17:12)] "and they followed those (chiefs) who, having been given wealth and children, have only increased in ruin." This wealth and these children deceived them and led them further astray. Consequently, through wealth and children, they received only misfortune and loss.

They did not stop at misguidance alone, but went further.

﴿And they schemed a mighty scheme﴾ (71:22). That is, they devised such a tremendous plot that no greater plot could come after it. They employed cunning to close off every path of the Islamic call. They diverted people's hearts toward other pursuits and eliminated every opportunity for the call to take root in their hearts. They made disbelief, misguidance and jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) appear attractive to them, and people continued to wander in jahiliyyah.

Their greatest deception was that they kept people busy worshipping the gods they had declared to be deities. They instilled in the common people a zeal and a sense of honour for these idols.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verse 23:**

﴿And they said: "Do not abandon your gods"﴾ [71:23]. They addressed these idols as "your gods" (*ilah*) so that their followers would be stirred up, so that a false zeal and a sense of honour that urges one toward sin would be awakened. Then they specifically mentioned those idols that were the most honoured and famous, so that the common people would rise up in their support.

﴿وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا﴾ ... ﴿"Nor leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr"﴾ [71:23]. This Nasr was their greatest idol, which was worshipped even in the days of ignorance (*jahiliyyah*) before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Misguided leaderships have always fashioned idols for the common people to worship. Only their names and forms vary from time to time, but the common people are made to revolve around them. An ignorant love for these idols is created in the hearts of the masses, so that they may drive the people into whatever pit of destruction they wish and cast them down. And they keep them upon this misguidance and keep them imprisoned within this misguided leadership.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verse 24:

﴿And they have led many astray.﴾ (17:42) Every misguided leadership gathers the masses before idols of this kind. These idols take the form of stones, they take the form of individuals, and they take the form of ideas. All of them are idols, and all of them block the path of the Islamic call. They keep the masses away from the bearers of truth. They hatch great conspiracies and insist upon those conspiracies.

At this point, a curse wells up from the heart of this Prophet (ﷺ) against these misguided, deceivers, and misleaders, and against their followers.

﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but error.﴾ (17:42) This is the curse of a heart that struggled for a long time and bore hardships for a long time. This curse came forth when all means had been exhausted and it became clear that in these wrongdoing, rebellious and defiant hearts not even a spark of goodness remained. It also became clear that these hearts no longer deserved the guidance and salvation of the Lord.

Before the complete supplication of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) is related here, the end of the wrongdoers and sinners is related: the end that befell them in this world, and also that which will befall them in the Hereafter. For from the standpoint of Allah's knowledge, the Hereafter is present and existent, and from another angle, its occurrence is so certain that it is as though it has already occurred.

Because of their sins, their wrongdoings and their disobedience, they were made to enter the Fire (Jahannam). Here the fa' of ta'qib is used with the sense of intention (fa' al-ta'qib bil-iradah). For as soon as they were drowned, they were also cast into Hell, and the time gap between their drowning and their entry into Hell is, as it were, no gap at all, since it carries no weight in the measure and standard of Allah. It is as though their being drowned in this world and their being made to enter the Fire in the Hereafter are close and continuous with one another. It is also possible that what is meant is the period of the punishment of the grave, which is extremely brief.

﴿And they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾ (17:52) — neither children, nor wealth, nor rank, nor friends, nor their so-called gods.

In these two short verses the story of these rebels is brought to an end, and their account of life is concluded. But the supplication of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), "O Allah, destroy them so that not even their existence remains," has not yet ended. The details of their drowning and the story of the flood are not given here, because the purpose at this point is to show the completion of their story with great swiftness. Thus the long interval between the drowning and the entry into Hell is folded up by the fa' of ta'qib alone.

Noah (peace be upon him) had received an inspiration in his heart that this impure earth was to be cleansed, and that the wrongdoers and rebels had filled it with evil and corruption. This evil had become so dominant and so deeply entrenched that it had rendered the call to religion stagnant, and the people of Noah's time had now become beyond reform. Often it happens that when the people of the earth become beyond reform, a general destruction comes upon them, and in this way Allah purifies the earth. This is the point to which Noah (peace be upon him) had arrived. Therefore he prayed: "O Allah, destroy these people, uproot the wrongdoers root and branch, let no living being remain," and he also gave his reasoning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 71, verse 27:

"If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants" (17:72). "Your servants" here refers to the believers. That is, the people would believe, but these influential, rebellious and powerful leaders would mislead them through their authority and strength. It may also refer to ordinary people in general. In that case the meaning is that these leaders would influence the common people through their rank and lofty position and turn them away from Allah.

Then these people created an atmosphere in which only disbelievers are born. Whatever children are born, a generation of disbelievers comes into being as a result of their birth, because the atmosphere the wrongdoers have prepared produces only a wrongdoing and misguided generation, one deprived of the light of faith. This is the reality to which Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) pointed, and which the Noble Quran related through his words.

"And they will not beget any but wicked and ungrateful disbelievers" (71:27). Because they spread corrupt and misguided conditions, practices and ideas in their society, and they have made their society and system such that only sinners and wrongdoers can come into being within it.

So Noah (peace be upon him) once again prayed for their destruction. Allah accepted his prayer and cleansed the face of the earth of their filth. A flood came upon them that swept away everything. Such a devastating flood can only be brought by Allah, the Compeller, the Subduer.

Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) prayed against the disbelievers that they be utterly destroyed. He said: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but destruction﴾ (17 : 82). On the other hand, he made supplication for himself: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and whoever enters my home as a believer, and the believing men and believing women﴾ (17 : 82).

Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) also called upon Allah for his own forgiveness. These are the etiquettes of the prophets before the Lord, the Exalted. A servant should speak humbly before Allah in the manner in which Nuh (peace be upon him) is speaking. He is making supplication the way a human being makes supplication. A human being commits mistakes and shortcomings. Although a prophet is extremely obedient to his Lord, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, that he himself could not enter Paradise except by the grace of his Generous Lord. Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) is a prophet. He struggled tirelessly for a long period, yet he still prays that Allah forgive whatever shortcomings occurred.

Then he prays for his parents. A prophet respects his parents. It is evident that they were believers. Had they not been believers, Allah would not have permitted him to do so, just as Allah did not hear his plea concerning his son, who was a disbeliever.

Then his supplication concerns those who sit in his household and in his society as believers.

This is the goodness of one believer toward another. A believer wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself. The mention of the household here is because, in that flood, there were commands for all the believers to enter the home of the Prophet, and he would carry them out in the ark (safinah).

After this, there is a supplication for the believing men and believing women in general. This too is the attitude of a prophet, that he holds good wishes for all the people of faith, whether they are of his own era, lived before him, or come in later ages. This is one of the secrets of the Islamic worldview (nazariyah-e-hayat): those who are linked with this worldview have very deep connection, relationship, love and brotherly feelings among themselves. And this distinction belongs to the Islamic worldview alone. Against this love, there is hostility and aversion toward the disbelievers.

﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers in anything but destruction﴾ (17 : 82). Here this surah concludes, in which, on one hand, there is a depiction of the tireless struggle of a noble prophet, and on the other hand, a depiction of the rebellious and hostile. This shows how great a struggle the callers to truth (du'at al-haqq) must undertake, how many difficulties arise on this path, and how great a sacrifice the movement of da'wah (the call to Islam) demands. This great struggle is necessary because no human society can achieve progress and success in this world and the Hereafter except through the da'wah of Islam and the Islamic system. In short, the secret of progress and the means of elevating humanity lie in the establishment of the da'wah of Islam and the Islamic system.
